1. Heard Sri Ram Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Nikhil Singh, learned AGA-I for the State and Sri Uma Shankar Verma, who has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of the informant/
prosecutrix.
Said Vakalatnama is taken on record.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant has filed supplementary affidavit, the same is taken on record.

3. As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant is in jail since 06.09.2024 in Case Crime No.293 of 2024, under Sections 376 & 419 IPC, Police Station ? Kotwali Tanda, District ?
Ambedkar Nagar.

At this Stage, learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the present informant is herself having her checkered history of exploiting the persons.

Attention has been drawn towards Annexure No.7 of the bail application, which is a compromise between the informant and one Anil Kumar Marya filed before the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Ambedkar Nagar on 12.11.2016.

entities.text: Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Ambedkar Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per aforesaid compromise, the informant is wife of one Anil Kumar Maurya.

Anil Kumar Maurya has filed one suit bearing Suit No.495 of 2012 before the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Ambedkar Nagar as questionnaire to that effect has been enclosed as Annexure No.8 with the bail application.
In the aforesaid case, the informant/complainant is opposite party.
So, learned counsel has stated that the informant is wife of one Anil Kumar Maurya at least since 2012.

5. Further attention has been drawn by the learned counsel for the applicant towards Annexure No.9 of the bail application, which is an FIR bearing Case Crime No.0717 of 2023, under Sections 3/4/5/6 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, P.S. Akbarpur, District- Ambedkar Nagar dated 25.12.2023 wherein the present informant and two others are accused persons.

Serious allegations have been levelled against the informant in such FIR wherein she has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 29.02.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.2383 of 2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.2383 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
While granting bail to the informant, condition no.(i) has been indicated in bold letters, which reads as under:-
"(i) The applicant shall appear once in a month before the local police station i.e.
Kotwali Akbarpur, district Ambedkar Nagar till expiry of one year from today i.e. till the end of February, 2025 to mark her presence in order to show that she has not indulged again in organization of prostitution or keeping a brothel house and, if the applicant is found involved again in the case of identical nature, the trial court,
without waiting any order from this court, would be justified to cancel the facility of bail granted to her by this court by initiating proceedings under section 439(2) CrPC.
6.

In the aforesaid FIR, name of the informant has been indicated as 'X' (name is concealed) wife of Santosh, therefore, learned counsel has stated that earlier the informant got married with one Anil Kumar Maurya and when she was arrested pursuant to the aforesaid FIR, she apprised herself as wife of Santosh and now she trapped the applicant since the present applicant was known to her,
therefore, she started blackmailing and under threat of arrest, the present applicant gave a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- to the informant by way of compromise deed dated 01.08.2024, which has been enclosed as Annexure No.10 to the bail application.
Therefore, learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the present applicant is himself victim of the malafide intention of the informant.
The present applicant is having no prior criminal history of any kind whatsoever.

Charge sheet has been filed, therefore, the applicant undertakes that if he is released on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order and shall cooperate in the trial proceedings.

7. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the complainant/ informant has, however, opposed the prayer for bail but they could not dispute the aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the applicant.

sentences.text: Without entering into merits of the issue; considering the arguments of learned counsel for the parties; contents and allegations of the FIR; the fact that the informant is herself having her checkered history of exploiting the persons as she is said to be the wife of one Anil Kumar Maurya at least since 2012 and one FIR was also lodged against her under Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act wherein she apprised herself as wife of Santosh; it appears that the present applicant is himself victim of the malafide intention of the informant as under threat of arrest, the present applicant gave a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- to the informant by way of compromise deed dated 01.08.2024; the applicant is having no prior criminal history of any kind whatsoever and undertaking of the applicant that he shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of bail, I find it appropriate to release the applicant on bail.
9. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

10. Let applicant- Ali Akbar be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v)The applicant shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
[Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.]
